name: claims
title: Claims
summary: A factual sentence in this repository is a claim: it carries the primary source it comes from and a check that it still holds, so the next reader, person or agent, can trust it without rebuilding the proof.

name: conformance
title: The conformance matrix
summary: Some review findings come back again and again: focus lost when a control disappears, server HTML that a reader in another time zone or locale cannot hydrate, a part on the wrong side in a right-to-left page, a control that vanishes under forced colours, a message announced twice.

name: forms
title: Forms
summary: A form control is one component on the Field contract: pass `label`, `name` and `error`, and wrap the controls in a `Form` that takes `errors` straight from your server action.

name: guardrails
title: Guardrails
summary: The guardrail kits hold an app to Ouro UI: the aim is that every control a person can reach is an Ouro control, and the number that are not can only fall.

name: installing
title: Installing
summary: Add `ouro-base` once per app, then add components; no later add changes your stylesheet or your test-tool versions.

name: screen-reader-lane
title: The screen-reader lane
summary: Ouro UI's components are read by real screen readers before every release: VoiceOver on macOS and NVDA on Windows, driven through Guidepup in this repository's CI.

name: static-css
title: Static CSS
summary: Ouro HX's tokens also come as plain stylesheets, for a page with no build step and no Tailwind: a status page, a report or a prototype written in HTML.

name: status-dashboards
title: Status dashboards
summary: A status dashboard tells a person where some work stands: what is done, what failed, what is running, and what nobody has started.

name: testing
title: Testing
summary: Ouro UI's tests install beside each component and run in your app, in real browsers, against your theme.

name: why-no-skill-app-shell
title: Comparison results: app-shell
summary: Comparison overview, scores, protocol and limits

name: why-no-skill-command-palette
title: Comparison results: command-palette
summary: Comparison overview, scores, protocol and limits

name: why-no-skill-confirm-delete
title: Comparison results: confirm-delete
summary: Comparison overview, scores, protocol and limits

name: why-no-skill-recipe-list
title: Comparison results: recipe-list
summary: Comparison overview, scores, protocol and limits

name: why-no-skill-settings-form
title: Comparison results: settings-form
summary: Comparison overview, scores, protocol and limits

name: why-no-skill
title: Why Ouro HX needs no skill
summary: Ouro HX puts component guidance in the source an agent already reads: required props, compiler hints and development messages.

name: can-share
title: canShare
summary: Whether the browser has a share sheet for this data: most phones and Safari do, most desktop browsers do not.

name: color-scheme-script
title: colorSchemeScript
summary: The script that sets the page's color scheme before it paints, so a reload in dark mode never flashes light.

name: copy-text
title: copyText
summary: Puts text on the clipboard: through the Clipboard API, or a text selection where the page may not use it (plain http, an older browser).

name: share
title: share
summary: Shares a link through the system's share sheet, or copies it where there is none, and says which happened.

name: use-color-scheme
title: useColorScheme
summary: The person's color scheme, the scheme the page shows, and the setter that changes both, for a control of your own.

name: claim
title: claim
summary: Marks a sentence of copy as a claim, with the primary source it comes from and a check that it still holds.

name: radio
title: Radio
summary: One choice in a `RadioGroup`, with its label to its right.

name: menu-bar
title: MenuBar
summary: A row of menus, as at the top of a desktop app: File, Edit, View.

name: menu-checkbox-item
title: MenuCheckboxItem
summary: An on/off setting in a `Menu`, with a check mark when it is on.

name: menu-group
title: MenuGroup
summary: Items under a label in a `Menu`, such as "Recipe" and "Account" sections.

name: menu-item
title: MenuItem
summary: One action in a `Menu`: `onClick` runs it, `href` makes it a link, `shortcut` shows its keys and `tone="destructive"` marks an action that cannot be undone.

name: menu-radio-group
title: MenuRadioGroup
summary: One choice of several in a `Menu`, such as a sort order: its `MenuRadioItem`s show a mark on the chosen one, and choosing keeps the menu open.

name: menu-radio-item
title: MenuRadioItem
summary: One choice in a `MenuRadioGroup`, marked when it is the group's value.

name: menu-separator
title: MenuSeparator
summary: A line between items in a `Menu`, to set apart a group of actions such as the destructive ones at the end.

name: menu-sub
title: MenuSub
summary: A nested menu in a `Menu`: an item that opens more items beside it, on hover, click or the arrow key.

name: buzz
title: buzz
summary: Vibrates the device in a short alert pattern, where it can (most Android phones; not iOS or desktops).

name: chime
title: chime
summary: Plays a short alert, three soft tones, for something that just finished: a timer at zero.

name: create-chime-context
title: createChimeContext
summary: Makes an audio context for `chime`, or returns `null` where the browser has no Web Audio.

name: format-duration
title: formatDuration
summary: Seconds as a clock reads them: `9:05`, or `1:02:03` from an hour up.

name: reset-timer
title: resetTimer
summary: Cancels or dismisses a timer by its timerId, including when its screen is not mounted.

name: restore-timer
title: restoreTimer
summary: Imports a saved countdown, leaving an existing native timer intact.

name: toast
title: toast
summary: Shows a toast: a short message that appears at the bottom of the screen, is read to screen readers once, and dismisses itself.

name: use-install-prompt
title: useInstallPrompt
summary: Whether the browser offers to install this web app, and the means to offer it at a good moment rather than when the browser chooses: `install()` opens the browser's own install dialog, `dismiss()` puts the offer away for two weeks.

name: use-timer
title: useTimer
summary: A countdown timer that keeps time by the clock, not by ticks, so it stays right in a background tab, across a reload (with `timerId`) and when the screen sleeps.

name: avatar-group
title: AvatarGroup
summary: Avatars stacked with a slight overlap, such as the cooks on a recipe, with a "+N" count after `max`.

name: resizable-handle
title: ResizableHandle
summary: The draggable line between two panels in a `ResizablePanelGroup`, a focusable window splitter (`role="separator"`) for the panel before it.

name: resizable-panel
title: ResizablePanel
summary: One resizable area of a `Resizable` (or `ResizablePanelGroup`), sized in percent of the group.

name: resizable-panel-group
title: ResizablePanelGroup
summary: A group of panels with handles you place yourself, shadcn's shape: `ResizablePanel` and `ResizableHandle` elements as direct children.

name: chart-container
title: ChartContainer
summary: shadcn's name for `Chart`: the same component with the same props, so code ported from shadcn's chart docs finds it.

name: chart-legend
title: ChartLegend
summary: The legend for a recharts chart inside `Chart`: each series' marker shape and label from the chart's `config`, under the plot.

name: chart-tooltip
title: ChartTooltip
summary: The tooltip for a recharts chart inside `Chart`: the category, then each series' marker, label and value from the chart's `config`, in the theme's popover colors.

name: color-scheme-provider
title: ColorSchemeProvider
summary: Keeps the page's color scheme: it applies the person's choice (`light`, `dark` or `system`) as the `.dark` class on `<html>`, which is how shadcn themes switch, keeps it in `localStorage`, and follows the system's setting live while the choice is `system`.

name: ouro-provider
title: OuroProvider
summary: Optional app-level provider that routes internal `href`s through your router's link and groups tooltips: once one `Tooltip` shows, its neighbours open instantly instead of each waiting its own delay.
